fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate the turn-in, especially at night or in low visibility.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Clear overhanging branches above the driveway to allow full-height emergency vehicles to travel the full length without restriction.
• Create or designate a turnaround area near the main residence so fire and emergency vehicles can reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Mark the edges of any existing turnaround area with visible markers so responders can identify usable limits in low visibility conditions.
• Keep the area around the detached structure clear of vehicle parking so responders have direct access to all sides.
• Post a secondary address marker or directional sign at any point where the driveway forks or changes direction.
• Thin dense vegetation immediately surrounding the main residence so responders can move around the building on foot without obstruction.
• Keep a gate, if present at the driveway entrance, unlocked or provide a key box accessible to emergency responders.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between tree canopies and the building.
• Cut or mow grass growing close to the structure down to a short height.
• Remove shrubs growing beneath tree canopies near the structure to reduce connected vegetation between ground and trees.
• Clear any dead or dry grass and shrub material from around the base of the structure.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of overhanging branches to allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Trim back shrubs and grass along both edges of the driveway so the travel surface remains fully passable.
• Remove shrubs or tall grass that limit visibility along driveway curves or at the driveway entrance.
• Keep the single access route free of fallen branches, debris, or encroaching vegetation that could block a vehicle in an emergency.
• Maintain a clear turning or passing area near the structure so emergency vehicles can maneuver without backing out the full length of the driveway.
• Separate clusters of shrubs near the structure by thinning or removing individual plants to break up continuous patches of vegetation.
